lehigh-2005-02.title: Set up an equation
lehigh-2005-02.body:
Let the second number be $x$. Then $2x+x+(x+5)=17$, so $4x=12$ and $x=3$. The numbers are $6,3,8$.

**Answer: 8**

lehigh-2005-03.title: Track the acid
lehigh-2005-03.body:
Adding $x$ cc of pure acid: $\frac{20+x}{100+x}=\frac13$, so $x=20$. Now there are $40$ cc of acid in $120$ cc. For 20% acid the total must be $40/0.2=200$ cc, so add $200-120=80$ cc of water.

**Answer: 80 cc**

lehigh-2005-04.title: Altitude to the base
lehigh-2005-04.body:
The altitude to the side of length $12$ splits it into two parts of $6$, so $h=\sqrt{10^2-6^2}=8$. Area $=\frac12\cdot12\cdot8=48$.

**Answer: 48**

lehigh-2005-06.title: Area two ways
lehigh-2005-06.body:
The hypotenuse is $13$. The area is $\frac12\cdot5\cdot12=\frac12\cdot13\cdot h$, so $h=\frac{60}{13}$.

**Answer: $\frac{60}{13}$**

lehigh-2005-07.title: Common exponent
lehigh-2005-07.body:
All exponents are multiples of $6$. Taking 6th roots gives $1^8,2^7,3^6,4^5,5^4,6^3,7^2,8^1,9^0$, i.e. $1,128,729,1024,625,216,49,8,1$. The largest is $4^5=1024$, which corresponds to $4^{30}$.

**Answer: $4^{30}$**

lehigh-2005-08.title: Total time
lehigh-2005-08.body:
The bicyclists close the gap at $19$ mph, so they meet after $\frac{2}{19}$ hour. The fly flies the whole time at $12$ mph: $12\cdot\frac2{19}=\frac{24}{19}$ miles.

**Answer: $\frac{24}{19}$ miles**

lehigh-2005-10.title: Count diagonals
lehigh-2005-10.body:
An $n$-gon has $\binom n2-n=\frac{n(n-3)}2$ diagonals. For $n=11$: $\frac{11\cdot8}{2}=44$. For $n=10$ it is $35$ and for $n=12$ it is $54$, so $45$ is not attained.

**Answer: 11**

lehigh-2005-11.title: Count ordered draws
lehigh-2005-11.body:
There are $5\cdot4=20$ ordered draws. Both red: $2\cdot1=2$; both black: $3\cdot2=6$. Probability $=\frac8{20}=\frac25$.

**Answer: $\frac25$**

lehigh-2005-12.title: Triangle inequality
lehigh-2005-12.body:
The base must be positive: $3x-2>0$, so $x>\frac23$ (then the legs are positive too). The triangle inequality requires the base to be less than the sum of the legs: $3x-2<2(x+1)$, so $x<4$. The other inequalities hold automatically.

**Answer: $\frac23<x<4$**

lehigh-2005-13.title: Count by generations
lehigh-2005-13.body:
After each generation of blasts the pieces have mass $\frac{2000}{3^k}$. Pieces of generation $k$ weigh more than $20$ kg while $3^k<100$, i.e. $k\le4$ (mass about $24.7$ kg for $k=4$). So generations $0,1,2,3,4$ each need a blast per piece: $1+3+9+27+81=121$ blasts. This leaves $243$ pieces of about $8.2$ kg, each needing one blast to become dust: $243$ more.

Total: $121+243=364$.

**Answer: 364**

lehigh-2005-14.title: Diameter along the line of centers
lehigh-2005-14.body:
The centers are $(0,0)$ and $(1,2)$, at distance $\sqrt5$; the radii are $1$ and $2$. The smallest enclosing circle has as a diameter the segment along the line of centers from the far point of one circle to the far point of the other, of length $1+\sqrt5+2$. So the radius is $\frac{3+\sqrt5}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}$**

lehigh-2005-15.title: Place digits in turn
lehigh-2005-15.body:
The digits are $0,3,3,3,4,5,5$. The $0$ can go in any of $6$ non-leading places. The three $3$'s then go in $\binom63=20$ of the remaining $6$ places, the two $5$'s in $\binom32=3$ of the remaining $3$, and the $4$ is forced. Total $6\cdot20\cdot3=360$.

**Answer: 360**

lehigh-2005-15.title: Subtract leading zeros
lehigh-2005-15.body: All arrangements: $\frac{7!}{3!\,2!}=420$. Those starting with $0$: $\frac{6!}{3!\,2!}=60$. Difference $360$.

lehigh-2005-16.title: Translate to base 10
lehigh-2005-16.body:
In base $b$: $4(b+2)=b^2+3$, so $b^2-4b-5=0$, i.e. $(b-5)(b+1)=0$. The positive solution is $b=5$.

**Answer: 5**

lehigh-2005-17.title: Two pyramids
lehigh-2005-17.body:
Let the cube have side $1$. The octahedron is two square pyramids sharing a base: the four side-face centers form a square (the common base) with side $\frac{\sqrt2}2$ and area $\frac12$. Each pyramid has height $\frac12$, so its volume is $\frac13\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac12=\frac1{12}$. The octahedron has volume $\frac16$, so the ratio is $6$.

**Answer: 6**

lehigh-2005-18.title: Add pieces cut by cut
lehigh-2005-18.body:
The $k$-th cut can cross the $k-1$ earlier cuts at distinct points inside the pizza, which splits it into at most $k$ new pieces. So the maximum is $1+(1+2+\cdots+9)=1+45=46$.

**Answer: 46**

lehigh-2005-19.title: Find the pattern
lehigh-2005-19.body: The group sums are $1,8,27,64$, the cubes. In fact group $i$ has $i$ numbers with average $i^2$, so its sum is $i^3$. For $i=10$: $1000$.

lehigh-2005-19.title: Direct
lehigh-2005-19.body:
Before the tenth group there are $1+2+\cdots+9=45$ odd numbers, so the tenth group runs from the $46$th odd number $91$ to the $55$th, $109$. Ten terms with average $100$ give $1000$.

**Answer: 1000**

lehigh-2005-21.title: Sum and product of roots
lehigh-2005-21.body:
The student who miscopied the middle term had the correct constant term, so $c=2\cdot3=6$. The student who miscopied the constant term had the correct middle term, so $-b=2+5=7$, $b=-7$. The equation is $x^2-7x+6=0=(x-1)(x-6)$.

**Answer: $\{1,6\}$**

lehigh-2005-22.title: Half the diagonal
lehigh-2005-22.body:
The center of the square is at distance $\sqrt2$ from each vertex (half the diagonal $2\sqrt2$). The small circle is externally tangent to the unit circles, so $1+r=\sqrt2$ and $r=\sqrt2-1$.

**Answer: $\sqrt2-1$**

lehigh-2005-23.title: Expand and compare
lehigh-2005-23.body:
$(x+i)^4=x^4+4ix^3-6x^2-4ix+1$. Setting this equal to the given left side leaves $6ix^3-6ix=4ix^3-4ix$, so $2ix^3-2ix=0$, i.e. $2ix(x-1)(x+1)=0$.

**Answer: $x=0,1,-1$**

lehigh-2005-24.title: Solve for the legs
lehigh-2005-24.body:
Let the legs be $x\le y$: $xy=16$, $x^2+y^2=64$. Then $(y+x)^2=96$ and $(y-x)^2=32$, so $y+x=4\sqrt6$, $y-x=4\sqrt2$. The tangent of the smallest angle is $\frac xy=\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}=\frac{\sqrt3-1}{\sqrt3+1}=\frac{(\sqrt3-1)^2}{2}=2-\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $2-\sqrt3$**

lehigh-2005-25.title: Trailing zeros of 100!
lehigh-2005-25.body:
$100^{100}$ ends in $200$ zeros, far more than $100!$ does, so the number of trailing zeros of the difference equals that of $100!$. Factors of $5$ in $100!$: $\lfloor100/5\rfloor+\lfloor100/25\rfloor=20+4=24$, and there are plenty of $2$'s. So $24$ zeros.

**Answer: 24**

lehigh-2005-26.title: Acute triangle condition
lehigh-2005-26.body:
The longest side is $24$ or $n$. If $n\le24$ we need $24^2<10^2+n^2$, i.e. $n^2>476$, so $n\ge22$. If $n>24$ we need $n^2<10^2+24^2=676$, so $n<26$. Also $n<34$ for a triangle. Thus $n=22,23,24,25$: four values.

**Answer: 4**

lehigh-2005-27.title: Shift and subtract
lehigh-2005-27.body: Write the terms as $F_n/5^n$ with $F_1=F_2=1$, $F_n=F_{n-1}+F_{n-2}$. Split off the first two terms: $S=\frac15+\frac1{25}+\sum_{n\ge3}\frac{F_{n-1}+F_{n-2}}{5^n}=\frac6{25}+\frac15\left(S-\frac15\right)+\frac1{25}S$. So $\frac{19}{25}S=\frac6{25}-\frac1{25}=\frac15$ and $S=\frac5{19}$.

lehigh-2005-27.title: Generating function
lehigh-2005-27.body:
The numerators are Fibonacci numbers $F_n$ and $\sum F_nx^n=\frac{x}{1-x-x^2}$. With $x=\frac15$: $\frac{1/5}{1-1/5-1/25}=\frac{1/5}{19/25}=\frac5{19}$.

**Answer: $\frac5{19}$**

lehigh-2005-28.title: Remove the even terms
lehigh-2005-28.body:
The even terms sum to $\sum(2k)^{-4}=\frac1{16}A$. So $B=A-\frac A{16}=\frac{15}{16}A$, giving $\frac AB=\frac{16}{15}$.

**Answer: $\frac{16}{15}$**

lehigh-2005-29.title: Isosceles triangle
lehigh-2005-29.body:
Let $AB=1$, so $BC=2$ and $CE=2$, $CM=1=CD$. Triangle $CMD$ is isosceles with apex angle $\angle MCD=90^\circ-60^\circ=30^\circ$, so $\angle CMD=\frac{180^\circ-30^\circ}2=75^\circ$.

**Answer: 75**

lehigh-2005-30.title: Unroll the cylinder
lehigh-2005-30.body:
Unroll the cylinder: the circumference is $4\pi$. The path consists of a straight segment from height $6$ to height $2$ going once around (horizontal $4\pi$, vertical $4$), then one from height $2$ to $0$ going once around (horizontal $4\pi$, vertical $2$). Lengths: $\sqrt{(4\pi)^2+4^2}=4\sqrt{\pi^2+1}$ and $\sqrt{(4\pi)^2+2^2}=2\sqrt{4\pi^2+1}$.

**Answer: $4\sqrt{\pi^2+1}+2\sqrt{4\pi^2+1}$**

lehigh-2005-31.title: Stewart's theorem (law of cosines)
lehigh-2005-31.body:
Let $CD=x$ and $\theta=\angle BDC$. Law of cosines in $BDC$: $25=x^2+9-6x\cos\theta$. In $ADC$ (angle $180^\circ-\theta$ at $D$): $36=x^2+1+2x\cos\theta$. Multiply the second equation by $3$ and add the first: $3\cdot36+25=3(x^2+1)+(x^2+9)$, i.e. $133=4x^2+12$. So $x^2=\frac{121}{4}$, $x=\frac{11}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{11}{2}$**

lehigh-2005-32.title: Factor and use divisibility by 3
lehigh-2005-32.body:
Expand: $n!=m!(m!-2)$, so $n(n-1)\cdots(m+1)=m!-2$ (note $n>m$). Checking $m=1,2$ gives no solution, so $m\ge3$ and $3\mid m!$, hence $m!-2$ is not divisible by $3$. A product of three consecutive integers is divisible by $3$, so the left side has at most two factors: $n=m+1$ or $n=m+2$.

- $n=m+1$: the product is just $m+1$, so $m+1=m!-2$, i.e. $m!=m+3$; only $m=3$ works ($6=6$).
- $n=m+2$: $(m+2)(m+1)=m!-2$, i.e. $m!=m^2+3m+4$; $m=3$: $6$ vs $22$, $m=4$: $24$ vs $32$, $m=5$: $120$ vs $44$ and $m!$ grows faster, so no solutions.

So $m=3$, $n=4$: check $4!+1=25=(6-1)^2$.

**Answer: $(3,4)$**

lehigh-2005-33.title: Tangent subtraction formula
lehigh-2005-33.body:
Let the bisector have slope $x$ (tangent of its angle). The angle from slope $1$ to the bisector equals the angle from the bisector to slope $7$: $\frac{x-1}{1+x}=\frac{7-x}{1+7x}$. This gives $7x^2-6x-1=-x^2+6x+7$, i.e. $8x^2-12x-8=0$, so $x=2$ or $x=-\frac12$. The acute angle's bisector is the one lying between the lines, slope $2$ (the other is the bisector of the supplementary angle).

**Answer: 2**

lehigh-2005-34.title: Distribute prime exponents
lehigh-2005-34.body:
$4000=2^5\cdot5^3$. Distribute the exponent of $2$ among $x,y,z$: the number of solutions of $a+b+c=5$ in nonnegative integers is $\binom72=21$. For $5$: $d+e+f=3$ has $\binom52=10$ solutions. Total $21\cdot10=210$.

**Answer: 210**

lehigh-2005-35.title: Compute the radius
lehigh-2005-35.body:
Let the triangle have side $1$ and the circles radius $r$. Along the base: $2(n-1)r+2\sqrt3\,r=1$ (look at the $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle from a vertex to the nearest circle center), so $r=\frac1{2(n+\sqrt3-1)}$. There are $\frac{n(n+1)}2$ circles, covering area $\frac{n(n+1)}2\cdot\frac{\pi}{4(n+\sqrt3-1)^2}\to\frac\pi8$. The triangle has area $\frac{\sqrt3}4$, so the limit is $\frac{\pi/8}{\sqrt3/4}=\frac{\pi}{2\sqrt3}=\frac{\pi\sqrt3}6$.

**Answer: $\frac{\pi\sqrt3}{6}$**

lehigh-2005-36.title: Divisibility by 315
lehigh-2005-36.body:
We need $315=5\cdot7\cdot9$ to divide $579000+abc$. Since $579000=315\cdot1838+30$, we need $abc\equiv-30\equiv285\pmod{315}$. The 3-digit values are $285$, $600$, $915$.

**Answer: $285,600,915$**

lehigh-2005-37.title: Subtract areas
lehigh-2005-37.body:
Let $OX=x$. The quarter circle has area $\frac\pi4$. The region is the quarter circle minus triangle $OBX$ (area $\frac x2$) minus the region $XAD$, which is sector $AOD$ (area $\frac\pi{12}$) minus triangle $OAX$ (area $\frac12x\sin30^\circ=\frac x4$). So the area is $\frac\pi4-\frac x2-\frac\pi{12}+\frac x4=\frac\pi6-\frac x4$. Setting this equal to $\frac\pi8$ gives $\frac x4=\frac\pi{24}$, so $x=\frac\pi6$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi6$**

lehigh-2005-38.title: Power of a point
lehigh-2005-38.body:
Let the triangle be $ABC$ with $D,E$ the midpoints of $AB$, $AC$, and let the line $DE$ meet the circle at $G$ (beyond $D$) and $F$ (beyond $E$). By symmetry $GD=EF$. Power of the point $D$: $DA\cdot DB=DG\cdot DF$. If $s$ is the side of the triangle, $DA=DB=DE=\frac s2$ (midline), so $DE^2=EF\,(DE+EF)$. With $x=DE/EF$: $x^2=x+1$, so $x=\frac{1+\sqrt5}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}$**

lehigh-2005-39.title: Digit equations
lehigh-2005-39.body:
Write $n+m=10x+y$ and $n-m=10y+x$. Then $2n=11(x+y)$ and $2m=9(x-y)$, so $n$ is a multiple of $11$ and $m$ a multiple of $9$. With $10\le m<n$ and $m+n\le99$ the pairs are $(22,18),(33,18),(33,27),(44,18),(44,27),(44,36),(55,18),(55,27),(55,36),(66,18),(66,27),(77,18)$: twelve pairs. A brute-force check agrees.

**Answer: 12**

lehigh-2005-40.title: Distances from the center
lehigh-2005-40.body:
Let the circle have radius $r$ and let the chords be at distances $d_1$ and $d_2$ from the center: $36+d_1^2=r^2=64+d_2^2$. If the chords are on opposite sides of the center, $d_1+d_2=7$, so $7(d_1-d_2)=28$ and $d_1-d_2=4$, giving $d_1=\frac{11}2$, $d_2=\frac32$, $r^2=\frac{265}4$. (Same side would force a negative distance.) The middle chord is at distance $\frac{d_1-d_2}2=2$ from the center, so half its length is $\sqrt{\frac{265}4-4}=\frac{\sqrt{249}}2$ and the chord is $\sqrt{249}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{249}$**
